objective: By the end you can follow one site day from Ravi's first WhatsApp message to the owner's evening report, and say what each kind of record is for: attendance, work done, material used, money spent, and the day's conditions.

scenes.title: A day on site
beats: Seven months in. The Main block is up to its parapet. At the Annex, the footings are cast, and today the plinth beam goes on.
Monday, a quarter to eight. Ravi counts heads at the Annex: Manoj the mason, Satheesh the plumber, Vinod, and four helpers from Rahim's crew. Seven people.
By nine tonight, Ramesh and Doctor Krishnan will each have a report of this day. Ravi will not write it. He will only talk.

lines.text: From the first message to the 9 pm report

scenes.title: Five records, and what each one protects
beats: A site day leaves five kinds of record. Each one protects something.
Attendance protects the wages: pay for the people who came, and only them.
Work done protects the bill. It is counted on its BOQ line, and at the month's end, the client pays for exactly that.
Material used protects the stock. What came, minus what was used, is what should still be there.
The day's small spends protect the petty cash: tea, diesel, nails. Small, every day, and gone by the month's end if nobody writes them.
And the day's conditions: rain, hours lost, a machine down. They explain a slow day, today and when someone asks why the job was late.

steps.text: Wages: pay for who came, and only them
The bill: counted on its BOQ line

Why a day was slow: rain, hours lost, breakdowns

footer.text: Written the same day, they are facts. Remembered later, they are guesses.

scenes.title: Who came
beats: At five past eight, Ravi tells Mesiri who came. He types it the way he would say it.
Mesiri does not save anything yet. It sends back a card: the three people it found in the worker register, by name, and Rahim's crew as a count of four.
Ravi checks it and taps Save. That is the attendance. Nobody copies a register into Excel on Saturday.

scenes.title: Before the concrete covers it
beats: At half past twelve the beam's steel is tied, and the concrete goes in after lunch. Once it does, nobody will see that steel again.
So Ravi sends a photo. Mesiri keeps it with today's work on the plinth beam.
If anyone later asks how many bars went in, or the client wants to see his foundations, the answer is a photo with a date on it, not a memory.

scenes.title: What was done, and what it took
beats: At twenty to six, the beam is done. Ravi is tired, and he does not type. He sends a voice note, in Malayalam. Mesiri hears it as these words.
Mesiri understands it and answers with one card. The work: twenty-four running metres of plinth beam. The material used: ten bags of cement, aggregate, sand, and a hundred and twenty kilos of steel.
And the six hundred and fifty rupees he spent on tea for the crew.
One message, one tap. Three records: the work, the material and the spend.

scenes.title: A problem, said the same day
beats: At the Main block, the day went differently. Only two bags of cement were left this morning, and the conduit work stopped halfway.
Ravi says so, and asks for a hundred bags.
Mesiri makes it a request for material, waiting for Anil in the office. Tomorrow morning it is the first thing he sees. That is the next episode.

scenes.title: A slow day, explained
beats: Not every day goes to plan. Eight days later, it rains on all four sites from eleven, and four hours are lost.
Ravi says so, with the work that did get done: nine square metres of block work at the Annex, half a normal day.
Without that line, the half day looks like a slow crew. With it, the report says rain. And months later, when someone asks why the job ran late, the rain is on record, day by day.

scenes.title: The same day, entered in the office
beats: Not every site has a phone that works all day. When Ravi calls the office instead, Anil can put the same day in on the website.
On Attendance, he picks the Annex and the day, and ticks who came: Manoj, Satheesh, Vinod. Rahim's crew goes in as a count: four.
He saves, and it is the same record Ravi's message would have made: the same wages, the same report.
One record, two ways in. The site talks on WhatsApp; the office types on the website. Mesiri never counts it twice.

scenes.title: Who does what with the day
beats: Who does what with Ravi's day?
Ravi only reports. Three messages, at the times things happen.
Anil sees the request and the problem, and orders. Meera sees the attendance that will become wages, and the petty cash.
Ramesh reads the evening report. And Doctor Krishnan, the client, gets it too, every evening, without asking.

footer.text: The site talks once. Everyone else reads.

scenes.title: Every site's day, as it happens
beats: In the office, every Save lands on Today, as it happens.
All four sites of both projects have reported. Each one shows its workers, its work and its material, in the engineer's own words.
And the problems come first: cement at the Main block, before anyone has picked up a phone.

scenes.title: What should still be there
beats: Every use Ravi reported comes off the stock, site by site.
The Annex: the cement, steel and sand it used today are gone from its count, and what is left is what Ravi should find tomorrow morning.
The Main block: no cement. Red, below its least of a hundred bags. The count says what Ravi said, without anyone counting bags.

scenes.title: Nine o'clock: the day, on one page
beats: At nine, Mesiri makes the day's report for each project, on the company's letterhead. Nobody writes it.
The people on site, by trade and by contractor. The work done, with its quantities. The material that came, was used, and is left.
The open problems, the weather, and tomorrow's plan, taken from what Ravi said.
It goes to Ramesh and to Doctor Krishnan on WhatsApp. A site that did not report is shown as not reported, never left out quietly.

scenes.title: Five ways a site day is lost
beats: Five ways a site day is lost.
Reported tomorrow, from memory: the numbers are guesses, and nobody can check them.
A crew counted as six when four came. Two days' wages for nobody, every day, all year.
Material used but not said: the stock on paper is more than the stock on site, and nobody knows where it went.
Tea and diesel in a pocket diary. And a problem said only on the phone: nobody writes it down, so nobody owns it.

scenes.title: Three questions
beats: Three questions. Pause, and answer them before you go on.
One: what does attendance protect, and what does work done protect? Attendance protects the wages. Work done protects the bill.
Two: Ravi's voice note became three records. Which? The work on its BOQ line, the material off the stock, and the spend in the petty cash.
Three: who gets the day's report, and who writes it? Ramesh and the client get it at nine. Nobody writes it: Mesiri makes it from what Ravi said.
